This first bail application under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (equivalent to Section 439 of Cr.P.C.) has been filed by the applicant Galiya S/o Dubaliya Gaamad for grant of regular bail, who has been arrested on 14/06/2024 in connection with Crime No.313/2024, date (not mentioned) registered at Police Station Petlawad, District Jhabua (M.P.) for commission of offences under Sections 363, 366(A) and 376(2)(N) of Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 5(L)/6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present crime.

sentences.text: In this case, the statement of prosecutrix has been recorded before the trial Court, however, she has not supported the prosecution case and has turned hostile.
The age of the prosecutrix is estimated by the trial Court as 20 years at the time of recording her statement.
Applicant is a young person of 21 years of age.

He has no criminal antecedent and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:12371 2 MCRC-17143-2025 is in jail since 14/06/2024, meaning thereby, he has suffered jail incarceration of approximately eleven months.
Conclusion of trial will take sufficient long time.
Under these circumstances, counsel prays for grant of bail to the applicant.
4. Learned Deputy Govt. Advocate appearing for the respondent /
State has opposed the application and prayed for its rejection.

sentences.text: 5. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

6. After considering all the aspects and looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, rival submissions of the counsel for the parties and also looking to the period of custody and the fact that prosecutrix has not supported the prosecution case, without commenting on the merits of the case,
this application is allowed.

7. It is directed that the applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety to the satisfaction of the trial court for securing his presence before the said Court on all the dates of hearing fixed in this regard during trial.

It is also directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 480(3)
of BNSS.
8.

This order shall remain effective till the end of the trial, but in case of bail jump and breach of any of the precondition of bail, it shall become ineffective and cancelled without reference to this Bench.
